simulation_requirement:
# Prompt

Con la informacion disponible hasta el 13 de julio de 2024, predecir quien ganara la final de la Copa America 2024 entre Argentina y Colombia.

Responder exclusivamente en espanol.

La respuesta debe:

- elegir un unico ganador esperado;
- justificar la prediccion usando solo evidencia del contexto entregado;
- mencionar los principales factores de incertidumbre;
- no usar informacion posterior al 13 de julio de 2024.

Formato esperado:

Ganador predicho: Argentina o Colombia

Justificacion:
- evidencia 1
- evidencia 2
- evidencia 3

Incertidumbre:
- factor 1
- factor 2

Tambien devolver una salida estructurada JSON con:

- `predicted_winner`: Argentina o Colombia.
- `confidence`: numero entre 0 y 1.
- `winner_probability_point`: probabilidad puntual del ganador elegido.
- `winner_probability_range`: rango estrecho para el ganador elegido, con `winner_min` y `winner_max`.
- `predicted_goal_margin`: diferencia esperada de goles para el ganador, con valor puntual y rango.
- `probability_calibration`: explicacion breve de como se eligieron la confianza y los rangos.
- `probability_drivers`: factores que suben o bajan la probabilidad de cada equipo, con `source_id`.
- `justification`: claims con `source_id`.
- `uncertainty`: factores con `source_id`.
- `evidence`: claims principales con `source_id`.

Reglas de calibracion:

- No usar un rango generico fijo para todas las corridas.
- El rango de probabilidad del ganador debe ser estrecho: `winner_max - winner_min <= 0.05`.
- `winner_probability_point` debe caer dentro de ese rango.
- Si no hay odds/modelos probabilisticos directos, expresar la incertidumbre bajando la confianza y explicandola, no usando un rango enorme.
- Si aparecen odds, modelos o mercados, anclar el punto medio a esa evidencia.
- La confianza debe cambiar cuando cambia la evidencia temporal.
- Evitar valores redondos repetidos salvo que esten justificados por las fuentes.
- La diferencia de goles debe ser una prediccion pre-partido, no el resultado real.

# Structured Copa America Forecast

- Cutoff: 2024-07-13
- Temporal package: T3_slim
- Model: meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct

Ganador predicho: Argentina
Confianza: 0.7

## Probability range
- Winner probability point: 0.475
- Winner range: 0.45 to 0.5

## Predicted goal margin
- Winner margin point: 1.0
- Winner margin range: 0.0 to 2.0
- Rationale: Based on the historical context and recent form of both teams, Argentina is expected to win by a margin of 1 goal, with a possible range of 0 to 2 goals.

## Probability calibration
- Method: Model signals and market odds
- Confidence rationale: The confidence level is set to 0.7 based on the strength of the evidence, including Argentina's historical dominance and recent form.
- Range rationale: The winner probability range is set to 0.45-0.5 based on the model signals and market odds, which suggest a slight advantage for Argentina.

## Probability drivers
- Argentina: Historical context [COPA_T3_SLIM_01]
- Argentina: Recent form [COPA_T3_SLIM_02]
- Argentina: Market odds [COPA_T3_SLIM_03]

## Justificacion
- Argentina has a strong historical record against Colombia in Copa America knockout-stage meetings. [SLIM_01]
- Argentina has been in good form recently, with a 2-0 win over Canada in the semifinals. [SLIM_02]
- The market odds favor Argentina to win the tournament, with a probability of around 47.6%. [SLIM_03]

## Incertidumbre
- Injuries to key players [SLIM_02]
- Colombia's strong recent form, including a 28-match unbeaten streak [SLIM_04]

## Evidence
- Argentina and Colombia have met 15 times in Copa America history, with 7 Argentina wins, 3 Colombia wins, and 5 draws. [SLIM_01]
- Lionel Messi played the full match against Canada after recent concerns around an adductor issue and looked fitter than in the quarter-final against Ecuador. [SLIM_02]
- FanDuel's market price implies Argentina has around a 47.6% chance of winning the tournament. [SLIM_03]

metadata.source_packet_text:
# Copa America 2024 final evidence package - Line 5 slim

Cutoff: 2024-07-13.

Use only the information below. Do not use the July 14 final score or any post-final reporting.

## COPA_T3_SLIM_01 - Match and historical context

Argentina and Colombia were scheduled to play the 2024 CONMEBOL Copa America final on July 14, 2024 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. Argentina entered as defending Copa America champion and reigning World Cup champion, with 15 Copa America titles. Colombia had one Copa America title, won in 2001.

Before the final, Argentina and Colombia had met 15 times in Copa America history: 7 Argentina wins, 3 Colombia wins and 5 draws. Argentina was unbeaten against Colombia in five Copa America knockout-stage meetings, including matches decided by penalty shootouts.

## COPA_T3_SLIM_02 - Recent form

Argentina reached the final by beating Canada 2-0 on July 9. Lionel Messi scored his first goal of the tournament and Julian Alvarez also scored. Reports noted that Messi played the full match after recent concern around an adductor issue and looked fitter than in the quarter-final against Ecuador.

Colombia reached the final by beating Uruguay 1-0 on July 10. Jefferson Lerma scored from a James Rodriguez corner. Colombia played more than half the match with 10 men after Daniel Munoz was sent off, but protected the lead under pressure.

## COPA_T3_SLIM_03 - Market and model signals

Pre-final betting markets listed Argentina as the 90-minute favorite at +105, Colombia at +360, and the draw at +190. Trophy-lift markets had Argentina at -200 and Colombia at +170. Another post-semifinal market had Argentina at -170 to win the tournament and Colombia at +130.

FanDuel summarized model signals before the final: Opta estimated Argentina winning in 90 minutes 50.4 percent of the time, a draw at 23.6 percent, and Colombia winning in 90 minutes 25.4 percent. MasseyRatings listed Argentina at 41 percent and Colombia at 31 percent. FanDuel's market price implied Argentina around 47.6 percent to win.

## COPA_T3_SLIM_04 - Team strengths and uncertainty

Argentina's core included Lionel Messi, Angel Di Maria, Emiliano Martinez, Cristian Romero, Rodrigo De Paul, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernandez, Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez. Colombia's core included James Rodriguez, Luis Diaz, Jhon Cordoba, Camilo Vargas, Davinson Sanchez, Jefferson Lerma, Richard Rios and Jhon Arias.

Colombia entered on a 28-match unbeaten streak, with its last defeat coming against Argentina in a 2022 World Cup qualifier. James Rodriguez had six assists in the tournament before the final. Argentina had conceded only one goal in the 2024 Copa America and was trying to win a third straight major tournament after Copa America 2021 and World Cup 2022.
